name: Lupin Ltd
title: Lupin Ltd - 500257 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 record quarter (revenue INR 8,277 cr, +32%) but management guided US sales to USD 250-280m per quarter and FY EBITDA margin to 24-25%, signalling a sharp step-down from Tolvaptan and Mirabegron generic competition.

summary.headline: Lupin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR 8,277 crore and EBITDA hit INR 2,464 crore (30% margin), but management guided to a sharper US slowdown ahead.
summary.overview: Lupin reported a record quarter with revenue from operations of INR 8,277 crore (up 32% YoY) and EBITDA excluding forex and other income of INR 2,464 crore (up 50% YoY, 30% margin, up 340 bps). Growth was broad-based across the US, India, Other Developed Markets, Emerging Markets and GIB, with ex-US organic growth above 20%. Management said Q2 onwards the US will moderate on Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, with quarterly US sales of USD 250-280 million, and it trimmed full-year EBITDA margin guidance to 24-25% from around 25%. Net cash fell to INR 2,831 crore from INR 4,636 crore after the VISUfarma acquisition closed.

segments.name: US
segments.commentary: Sales of USD 366 million, up 30% YoY in constant currency, driven by base volumes and partly offset by Mirabegron competition. FY27 US guidance is USD 1.1-1.2 billion, with management expecting USD 250-280 million per quarter over the next couple of quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 2,380 crore, up 13.9% YoY; diabetes grew 31.8% (1.8x category) and cardiac 1.2x category, while respiratory grew 6.9% vs category 11.3%. Chronic share rose to about 67% from about 65% in FY26; volume growth was 6.1%.

segments.name: Other Developed Markets (Europe, Canada, Australia)
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 1,149 crore, up 48% YoY, with Europe up 83% YoY. VISUfarma consolidation began this quarter. Management guides 10-20% growth over the next couple of years.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Sales of INR 990 crore, up 52% YoY. Brazil grew 117% YoY in local currency on Dapagliflozin and Empagliflozin launches.

segments.name: GIB
segments.commentary: Grew 40% YoY in the quarter, per management; no further detail given on the segment's drivers.

guidance_outlook: FY27 US revenue guided at USD 1.1-1.2 billion; US growth expected to resume from FY28.
Full-year high single-digit revenue growth reiterated.
Full-year EBITDA margin now guided at 24-25% (earlier around 25%), with management citing a gross margin reduction from geopolitically driven cost increases and Tolvaptan pricing.
Full-year R&D guided at about 8% of sales; full-year ETR guided at 27-28%.
Management expects India formulations to outperform IPM by 1.2-1.3x; plans about 20 India launches in FY27 vs 15 in FY26.
Europe guided at 10-20% growth; ROW markets expected to grow double digits.
capex_capacity: Pithampur Unit II: responses submitted; remediation on track. Ankleshwar and Somerset received EIRs and VAI status from US FDA during the quarter.

Apixaban 505(b)(2) approval goal date is September 2026, with Somerset as the filing plant; material commercial quantities expected from January 2027 and launch around summer 2027, 10-12 months ahead of generics.

More than 15 US filings planned this year, including at least seven in respiratory; Dulera filed; Spiriva Respimat filing expected this fiscal year; Ellipta-platform ANDA expected later this year; Luforbec green propellant filed in Europe.

Biosimilar and launch plan: Pegfilgrastim H2 FY27, Ranibizumab and Aflibercept in Europe and later US; Etanercept in calendar 2029. Management sees biosimilars ramping to a couple of hundred million dollars across US and Europe within three years.
Fluticasone nasal spray Rx approval expected this year, OTC in FY28; formulation in-house, API sourced externally, device from a third-party manufacturer.
demand_pricing: Tolvaptan: Apotex and Teva entered from Q2; one more entrant possible in September, making four players. Management expects pricing to fall and share to redistribute, with the market still growing (about 40% generic conversion).
Mirabegron: pressure already visible in Q1, with full-quarter impact from Q2.
Albuterol US share stabilised at about 16% (down from 19-20%); Tiotropium share about 38%, which management expects to hold.

Europe: Germany's higher rebate affects part of the portfolio, but Ranibizumab and Aflibercept biosimilars are no longer in AOK tenders, creating a branded opportunity; France is pushing biosimilar substitution.
Adjacencies (Diagnostics, Digital, OTC, CDMO) reduce EBITDA margin by about 1-1.5%; management expects them to break even over time, with Diagnostics breaking even next year.
Apixaban 505(b)(2) could reach a scale similar to Mirabegron or Tolvaptan, per management, with targeted channel entry before generics arrive in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Does the USD 1.1-1.2 billion US guidance form the base for the return to growth in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that FY28 growth is expected over the FY27 base of USD 1.1-1.2 billion.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the US guidance imply a step-down from Q1's USD 366 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Tolvaptan faces new entrants from Q2 (Apotex, Teva, possibly a fourth in September), and Mirabegron has a full-quarter impact from Q2, so management expects USD 250-280 million per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is a normalised gross margin given the 74.6% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Swaminathan said it depends on Tolvaptan volumes and realisations, competition, and price increases after geopolitical cost rises; Q1 benefited from carried-forward inventory, so margins are guided lower at 24-25% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the Apixaban 505(b)(2) opportunity be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could reach Mirabegron or Tolvaptan scale, targeting a few large channels ahead of FY29 generic entry, with approval goal date September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How big can biosimilars be across the US and Europe over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees a couple of hundred million dollars in revenue from Pegfilgrastim, Ranibizumab, Aflibercept and Etanercept, though it did not size each product.

qa_highlights.question: Could EBITDA margin fall below 20% in some quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Swaminathan said quarterly volatility is certain but declined to quantify it; R&D is at least a notch above peers and adjacency losses are a 1-1.5% drag.

risks_watch: US erosion from Tolvaptan (four entrants by September) and Mirabegron, with the quarterly run-rate falling to USD 250-280 million.
Gross margin pressure from geopolitically driven cost increases and price realisation; full-year EBITDA margin guided lower to 24-25%.
Apixaban 505(b)(2) approval (goal date September 2026) and launch timing ahead of FY29 generic entry.
Germany's higher rebate policy and European pricing pressure.
Adjacency losses (1-1.5% EBITDA drag) and volatility in quarterly margins; net cash has fallen after VISUfarma.
Pithampur Unit II remediation still open; Spiriva Respimat's P4 patent status affects the FY29 timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth breadth and the long-term pipeline, but cautious on near-term US earnings: management explicitly flagged a sharp Q2-onward step-down and trimmed margin guidance. It was evasive on quantifying adjacency losses, Apixaban differentiation, and US market sizing for the exclusive first-to-file pipeline, offering to follow up offline.

growth.why: Management reiterated high single-digit FY27 revenue growth, with FY27 US guidance of USD 1.1-1.2 billion and India launches (about 20 in FY27) backing it, but US quarterly sales are expected to moderate to USD 250-280 million from Q2 on Tolvaptan and Mirabegron competition, and EBITDA margin was cut to 24-25%.
